title: Redwood PLG quickstart discovery - Pioneer Data
summary: Discovery call for Pioneer Data evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Key concerns: latency, cost, data residency, SSO/KMS. Customer wants quickstart + free credits to validate time-to-first-token and run a 1M token benchmark. AE to share pricing and security pack; SE to run sample benchmark and provide quickstart guide and pilot account details.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
next_steps: Maya to send pricing sheet and quickstart links by 2026-03-05
Liam to provision trial / pilot account and sample benchmark plan by 2026-03-09
Customer to confirm pilot users and success criteria by 2026-03-06
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) to run latency/cost benchmarks week of 2026-03-09
action_items: Maya: Email pricing + quickstart + free credits instructions (due 2026-03-05)
Liam: Configure trial account, share sample benchmark script and run initial 100k token test (due 2026-03-08)
Aisha: Share security contact and SOC2 requirements doc (due 2026-03-06)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:05] Aisha (CTO): hi, Aisha here, CTO at Pioneer Data, we run a mix of customer analytics and internal ML services. ben and clara on the line too.
[00:12] Ben (ML Eng): hey; ben. we own model infra, mostly AWS, a couple of self-hosted endpoints for inference.
[00:18] Liam (SE): great, thanks. quick agenda — understand current stack, what success looks like, and how fast you can get to first token with Redwood.
[00:26] Clara (Security): and i'll focus on security and data residency questions.
[00:30] Maya (AE): perfect. so to start, what's your current latency and cost pain?
[00:36] Ben: right now we're using SageMaker endpoints for some models and a tiny k8s cluster for latency sensitive stuff. 99th perc tail is okay but cost is high, and autoscaling is noisy.
[00:44] Aisha: primarily concerned about predictability; we have spikes from customer events. cost per token is starting to eat into margins.
[00:51] Liam: makes sense. with Redwood you can start on hosted to validate, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private if you need VPC/on-prem. quick question: is data residency a hard requirement?
[01:00] Clara: yes — some customer data must stay in EU. also we need SSO (SAML), RBAC, and KMS integration for key management. SOC 2 is non-negotiable.
[01:08] Maya: we've got SOC2, SAML, KMS integrations; for Private we can do a VPC option and on-prem if necessary. we'll share the security pack.
[01:15] Ben: on the engineering side, time-to-first-token matters. how fast is the quickstart? can our product team get a token in dev in an afternoon?
[01:22] Liam: typically minutes. our PLG quickstart has SDKs, Postman snippets, and a sample app. most teams hit first token within 30-60 minutes. with free credits you can run a basic validation in a few hours.
[01:31] Aisha: that's good. Any gotchas with models — like quantization, latency tradeoffs?
[01:36] Liam: yes — tradeoffs: smaller quantized variants save cost but may have subtle quality deltas. we recommend starting with a curated open model; runtime chooses kernels and will auto quantize if you opt in. for strict latency SLOs Dedicated with pinned capacity helps.
[01:47] Ben: can we run our own model artifacts or do we have to use Redwood catalog?
[01:51] Maya: you can bring-your-own model (BYOM). Redwood supports onboarding customer models; the runtime will suggest kernel/quantization profiles and we can run a small benchmark.
[01:58] Ben: perfect. about benchmark — we'd like to run a 1M token throughput/lattice test to compare hosted vs Dedicated cost. how would that work?
[02:05] Liam: we can provide a sample benchmark script and run an initial 100k tokens to tune batching/KV cache settings, then escalate to 1M tokens in pilot. we'll capture latency P95/P99, tokens/sec, and unit cost.
[02:16] Aisha: do you have examples of customers who started on hosted and moved to Dedicated?
[02:20] Maya: yes, several. typical path: quickstart with hosted, validate quality and latency, then sign a reserved capacity for Dedicated if steady production load emerges.
[02:28] Clara: about logs and audit — we need audit trails for token-level access and retention controls.
[02:33] Liam: Redwood Console has per-route tracing, token-level cost/latency, and audit logs. for Private we can ship logs to your SIEM; for Hosted we provide retention controls and export.
[02:43] Ben: any limitations on streaming or function/tool calling? we heavily use streaming for chat.
[02:47] Maya: streaming and function calling are supported. minor transcription note: sometimes Fireflies transcribed our product names oddly, but functionality is full.
[02:55] Aisha: pricing — we need a rough estimate for a 100k qps-month workload and what a Dedicated reservation looks like.
[03:03] Maya: i'll send a pricing sheet; high level — hosted per-token, dedicated committed monthly with lower unit cost. will include burst policies and autoscale options.
[03:11] Ben: onboarding: how long is a pilot? can we use free credits to run the benchmark?
[03:15] Liam: yes, free credits for quickstart. typical pilot 2-4 weeks to run benchmarking and integration validation. pilot account will have sample quotas so you can validate end-to-end.
[03:25] Clara: SSO and KMS integration timelines? we need SAML set up and KMS for keys for Private.
[03:30] Liam: SAML is straightforward; we'll share our SAML metadata. KMS integration for Private or Dedicated (if you bring keys) may need a handshake with your security team; we'll include a checklist.
[03:40] Jon (Product): ok, success criteria from our side: 1) match current P95 latency within 10% for key flows, 2) 30% lower cost per token vs current infra, 3) SOC2 + SSO + KMS validated.
[03:52] Maya: great, we'll treat that as acceptance criteria for the pilot.
[03:56] Ben: any notes about model ops — versioning and rollouts?
[03:59] Liam: Redwood supports model versioning, canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallbacks to compatible variants. We'll document the API for rollouts.
[04:07] Aisha: final Q — data residency: if we start hosted in EU region, will logs or keys transit to US?
[04:13] Liam: for hosted, region selection keeps data in-region; keys live in your KMS for Private; we'll detail boundary conditions in the security pack.
[04:20] Maya: ok to recap next steps?
[04:22] Aisha: yes please.
[04:24] Maya: I'll send pricing, quickstart links, free credits instructions, and security pack by tomorrow. Liam will provision a pilot account and share benchmark script; we'll schedule the SE-led deep dive for the week of March 9th. Pioneer to confirm pilot users and success criteria.
[04:37] Ben: sounds good.
[04:39] Clara: thanks, bye.
[04:41] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-transcription (e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache) and filler words. References shared: "Quickstart guide (link)", "security-pack.pdf (link)", "benchmark-script.py (link)" — links to be included in follow up email.
